title: Sole-source dollar ceilings for the bid-solicitation exception
text: Under section 6(b), a contracting authority may enter into a contract without soliciting bids where the estimated expenditure does not exceed $25,000 for a goods contract; $100,000 for a contract for architectural, engineering or other services related to the planning, design, preparation or supervision of a construction, repair or restoration of a work; or $40,000 for any other contract. A cluster of awards to the same supplier that each sit just below one of these ceilings is a contract-splitting red flag.

title: Competitive-tendering thresholds under trade agreements
text: Canadian federal procurements at or above the applicable trade-agreement threshold must generally be openly and competitively tendered. The Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) sets goods and services thresholds for federal entities that are periodically adjusted; CETA and the WTO Agreement on Government Procurement set parallel thresholds for covered entities. Award values that repeatedly land just below the applicable threshold, or non-competitive awards above it without a documented limited-tendering reason, warrant review. This is a curated summary; verify the current threshold values against the official Treasury Board contracting policy notices.
